why: Headnote summarises a High Court's decision that an expired licence defeats the insurer's liability; adoption by the current court is not shown here.

span: Insurance Company is entitled to take a defence that the offending vehicle was driven by an unauthorised person or the person driving the vehicle did not have a valid driving licence
why: Headnote recognises the insurer's licence defence but a later part of the same headnote (outside this passage) allows pay-and-recover; the passage alone does not settle the outcome. Headnote confidence is capped.

span: Claim Petition u/s. 163A of the Act filed by the appellants against the owner of the vehicle
why: Concerns the maintainability of a s.163A claim where the deceased was the borrower of the vehicle, not a licence defect.

span: the offending vehicle did not have a valid permit for being operated in the State of Karnataka
why: The insurer's argument rests on a missing permit, a different condition from the driver's licence; it is a party submission.

span: We deem it just and fair to direct the Respondent
why: Court affirms that the insurer is absolved of liability because of invalid licences, yet directs it to pay the enhanced compensation under pay-and-recover; both appear in the same paragraph.

span: they were still bound to pay compensation to third parties
why: Describes S. Iyyapan on insurers' limited liability and third-party rights in a licence-category case; adoption by the current court is not shown here.

span: the insurer would be still liable to pay the compensation amount in the first instance with liberty to recover the same from the owner
why: The insurer's liability turns on whether the deceased travelled with his goods and on a valid policy, not on a driver's licence defect.
